summary: Soapstone Mtn, Somers CT: the 1929 fire tower is gone; a public observation tower on the summit, rebuilt after its 2014 closure, is open.

facts.status_note: The 1929 fire tower is gone. A public observation tower stands on the summit.

access.note: The state keeps the summit observation tower for public viewing, and lists the forest as open daily.

visit.trail_note: The blue-blazed Shenipsit Trail passes over the mountain.

events.note: State bought the summit land to erect a fire tower
Tower erected in the early summer of 1929; opened for operation in spring 1930
30-foot wooden observation tower closed in October 2014 after the state found it structurally unsafe
Blog says the state replaced the unsafe version in 2018
Blog says local citizens rebuilt the tower in 2019; the blog gives two dates for the replacement and they are not reconciled. Only the old columns and concrete were kept

corrections.why: The 30-foot (9.1 m) figure is for the wooden observation tower closed in 2014, not the 1929 fire tower. No source gives the fire tower's height.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The state bought the summit in 1927 to erect a fire tower; the tower was erected in 1929 and opened in 1930. The dates fit one timeline.
The 30-foot figure belongs to the wooden observation tower closed in 2014. DEEP says the original fire tower is long gone.

notes_for_editor: Rebuild dates conflict inside one blog: the state replaced the unsafe version in 2018, and local citizens rebuilt the tower in 2019. Both are recorded as events; the conflict is unresolved. The radar dome and Army claims come from one personal hiking blog (CTMQ) and are not confirmed elsewhere. The 2016 Journal Inquirer text is read through the Forest Lookouts reprint, not the original. 'climbable: true' is inferred from the summit tower being an open public observation tower; confirm on site before publishing. The record kind 'tower' now describes a recreational observation tower, not a lookout; an editor may want a note. Record coordinates 41.95899, -72.4131 match the USGS GNIS summit Soapstone Mountain (41.9589, -72.4131). The ExploreCT guide is script-rendered and had no readable text.
